Second Medical Opinion
Making informed and reliable decisions
The concept in a nutshell
In everyday life, we usually seek comprehensive 
advice before we make important decisions. But what 
about matters concerning health and illness? 
A second medical opinion allows you to expand your 
information base before planned operations and  
medical treatments – independently and neutrally. 
 
You will receive answers to the following questions: 
–	 Do I really need the proposed treatment  
or operation?
–	 How will my health and quality of life  
change afterwards?
–	 What are the advantages and disadvantages of  
the proposed treatment or operation?
–	 Are there alternative forms of treatment?
–	 What happens if I do this treatment or operation 
later, or not at all?
A second opinion can confirm the necessity of the 
intended treatment, or else point out other pos­
sibilities. However, you are always free to decide how  
you would like to proceed afterwards. In order to main­
tain neutrality, any potential treatment or operation  
will not be carried out by the second opinion doctor.
Seeking a second medical opinion is recommended 
before any major intervention – except in the event of 
an emergency.
A second opinion is not suitable if you are dissatisfied 
with your medical care or ongoing treatment. In this 
case, it is best to seek a direct personal conversation 
with your doctor.
What does that mean for you?
For persons insured with PRIVATE, SEMIPRIVATE, 
LIBERO or GENERAL Hospital Insurance,  
CONCORDIA bears the costs of a second medical 
opinion.
In this case, you can request a second opinion from the 
Lucerne Cantonal Hospital (LUKS) without consulting 
CONCORDIA. You will receive the second opinion 
from a chief physician or a senior physician – personally 
sent to you within 14 working days. Before planned 
medical treatments or operations, the LUKS offers  
second medical opinions in these fields:
–	 Abdominal surgery: e.g. oesophagus, stomach, 
intestine, liver, pancreas, kidney, adrenal glands, 
liver or kidney transplants, benign and malignant 
abdominal tumours, thyroid gland, obesity
–	 Breast diseases: e.g. benign and malignant  
breast tumours
–	 Cardiology
–	 Dermatology and allergology
–	 Ear, nose and throat surgery
–	 Endocrinology: e.g. diabetes, thyroid
–	 Gynaecology: e.g. uterus, ovaries
–	 Haematology
–	 Hand and plastic surgery
–	 Nephrology: e.g. renal insufficiency, dialysis
–	 Neurosurgery: e.g. cerebral aneurysm, benign and 
malignant brain tumours
–	 Ophthalmology: e.g. cataract, glaucoma
–	 Oral and maxillofacial surgery
–	 Orthopaedics: e.g. shoulder, elbow, hand, pelvis, 
hip, knee, ankle, foot
–	 Pneumology: e.g. COPD
–	 Thoracic surgery
–	 Urology: e.g. kidney, bladder, prostate, andrology
–	 Vascular surgery: e.g. venous disorders of the legs, 
arterial circulatory disorders of the legs, carotid  
stenosis, ailments with dialysis access
